fixtures: Files are MCP declaration snapshots, copied into the run's data/ folder. notes-plugin is a small plugin directory.

evals.name: three-vendor-mcp-json
evals.prompt: This is the .mcp.json our plugin ships to Claude Code, Codex and Copilot CLI: data/team-tools.mcp.json. Anything wrong with it?
evals.expected_output: docs-search is a URL entry with no type: Claude Code needs type to tell url entries (http/sse) apart from stdio, and Copilot needs it on remote servers, so add "type": "http". It also cannot work on Codex, which supports stdio only. fs uses "type": "local", Copilot's alias; use "type": "stdio", which every vendor understands. git has no type, which is fine for a command-based stdio server.
assertions: Flags that docs-search has no type field, which Claude Code needs for url-based entries
Recommends adding an explicit type (http or sse) to docs-search
Says docs-search will not work on Codex because Codex supports stdio servers only
Flags "type": "local" on fs as Copilot-only and recommends "type": "stdio"
Does not flag the git server's missing type as an error

evals.name: cursor-plugin-path
evals.prompt: My notes MCP server works when I install the plugin in Claude Code, but when I install the same plugin in Cursor the server never shows up. The plugin is in data/notes-plugin (it has a .mcp.json at the root). What am I missing?
evals.expected_output: Cursor's plugin format reads mcp.json at the plugin root, with no leading dot; Claude Code reads .mcp.json. The plugin only has .mcp.json, so Cursor finds no servers. Add a mcp.json (same content) at the plugin root and keep .mcp.json for Claude. The server declaration itself is fine.
assertions: Says Cursor's plugin format expects mcp.json at the plugin root with no leading dot
Recommends adding mcp.json while keeping .mcp.json for Claude Code
Does not blame the server's command, args or the stdio transport
Does not tell the user to move the declaration into .cursor/mcp.json as the plugin fix

evals.name: portable-clean
evals.prompt: Is data/search.mcp.json portable to Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Copilot CLI as-is?
evals.expected_output: Yes. It is a stdio server with "type": "stdio", the spelling every vendor understands, so it also works on Codex. The tools key is Copilot-only and the other vendors ignore it, so it is harmless.
assertions: Says the file is portable to all four vendors
Says "type": "stdio" is the right, portable spelling and does not suggest "local"
Says the tools key is Copilot-specific and ignored by the other vendors, rather than an error to remove
Does not say Codex cannot run this server
